text: Every Upstream test case gets exactly one Test ID, with each data-provider or `#[TestWith]` dataset counted separately.
Regenerating the Test Inventory for the same Baseline Pin gives an identical result.
Each entry is tagged with its Component, whether it is a unit or an integration test, and any backend it needs: SQLite, Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Redis, or none.
The Test Inventory covers `laravel/framework`, `laravel/ai`, `laravel/mcp` and `laravel/boost`.

The list of Test IDs, including datasets computed at runtime, matches what the test runner actually runs inside the Oracle at the Baseline Pin (`phpunit --list-tests` or the JUnit output, and Pest's equivalent). CI checks the two match.
Each entry records a normalised hash of its test body and dataset values (used by FR-7).
Component tags come from a written mapping of test directories to Components. The mapping is a Phase 0 deliverable, on a Protected Path, signed off by the Maintainer.
CI fails if a Ported Test has no Test ID, has one that isn't in the Test Inventory, or shares one with another Ported Test.
Xaravel Tests are labelled as such and never counted in the Conformance Rate.
A `skip` without a Skip Reason from the vocabulary fails CI.

CI checks every Skip Reason against its rule in §3, and fails on any that breaks it: - `blocked-by` must name a Component in a later Phase. - `intentional-divergence` must name an existing Divergence Record. - `php-only` must reference an approved Escalation. - `upstream-skip` must be confirmed by the Oracle. - `deferred` must name a backend or feature listed as post-alpha in §7.2. - `out-of-scope` must name a §7.1 Non-Goal ID (NG-N).
A test may be `quarantined` only with an open Escalation.

When more than one Skip Reason could apply, the Expectations File records exactly one, chosen in this order: 1. `upstream-skip`, because it is machine-verified. 2. One that keeps the test in the SM-1 denominator: `intentional-divergence`, then `blocked-by`, then `not-ported-yet`. 3. Only if none of those fits, one that excludes it: `php-only`, `deferred` or `out-of-scope`. When in doubt, the agent picks the reason that counts against conformance.
A `fail-known` entry blocks Epic acceptance, and the dashboard counts it separately from skips.
An unexpected failure fails CI.
An unexpected pass also fails CI.
A Story's change may modify Expectations File entries only for the Test IDs assigned to that Story. CI fails any change that touches other entries (FR-112).
Changing an entry from `pass` to anything else requires an approved Escalation.
The denominator shown is always the full count of Test ID × Backend Variant pairs.
The page shows the alpha gate figure (SM-1) next to the full Conformance Rate.
The page shows counts per Skip Reason, links each Intentional Divergence to its Divergence Record, and lists open Escalations and Quarantined tests.
It shows the history across commits, with a marker at each Baseline Pin change.
The dashboard updates on every push to the default branch.
Generating the expected values twice for the same Baseline Pin gives identical results.
The Oracle runs in a container, so contributors and agents don't need PHP installed.
The tool outputs a list of added, changed and removed Test IDs. A Test ID counts as changed when its Upstream test body or its dataset values differ between the two pins.
Added and changed Test IDs become backlog Stories, and removed ones are retired from the Expectations File.
A changed Test ID is reset to `not-ported-yet`, keeping a link to its previous Ported Test. A renamed test (same hash, new Test ID) carries its status and history over.
A Phase boundary is a freeze point: no new Epics start, and in-flight Epics either finish or pause. The Baseline Pin can change only at a freeze point.
Phase 1 Stories are not started until `PORTING.md` and the Divergence Records are merged.
`PORTING.md` is piloted in Phase 0 on a sample of Support and Collections tests, and revised from the pilot before Phase 1 starts.
Every Divergence Record states its test-adaptation rule as numbered clauses.
`PORTING.md` states the mechanical rule for translating PHP expressions in Upstream test inputs, including Blade templates, to TypeScript.
The harness has a fast mode that runs a sample, and a filter by Component or Test ID. The sample is chosen from a seed that the harness prints, so the same seed gives the same sample (NFR-7).
Its output is short and can be grepped, with one line per failing Test ID.
On a developer machine, tests whose backend isn't running are reported as not run. They don't count as failures and are never recorded in the Expectations File.
CI runs SQLite, Postgres and Redis as services. In CI, every Backend Variant for an alpha backend must actually run.

At least two reviewer agents, separate from the implementing agent, compare each Ported Test with its Upstream source. They check: - the assertions match the Upstream ones; - no expected value has been weakened; - no assertion has been removed unless a Divergence Record allows it; - every new Skip Reason is justified.
The review verdict and its findings are stored with the Story.
A rejected Story goes back to its implementer with the findings.
The implementing agent doesn't stub, fake or partly implement a Component just to make another Component's tests pass. Reviewers reject changes that do.

These paths are protected: - the harness and the Ratchet - the Test Inventory and the Skip Reason vocabulary - the PHPUnit-style matchers and `@xaravel/mockery` - Oracle fixtures - `PORTING.md` and the Divergence Records - CI configuration - `@xaravel/contracts`, once Phase 1 is accepted
CI fails any Story change that touches a Protected Path.
Protected Paths change only through Infrastructure Stories that the Maintainer approves.
Infrastructure Stories run in Phase 0, or after an approved Escalation.
A Ported Test that runs zero assertions fails.
A Ported Test's assertion count is at least the Upstream count recorded in the Test Inventory, unless a Divergence Record allows fewer.
The harness reports both counts for each Test ID.
Escalations are recorded with the Test IDs, the evidence and the decision the agent proposes, and they appear on the dashboard.
The agent goes on with other assigned Test IDs.
An Epic can't be accepted while it has open Escalations.
The Maintainer's decision is recorded, and becomes a Divergence Record or a Protected Path change where that applies.
Each Xaravel Test declares which FR consequence it verifies.
A Xaravel Component's Epic is accepted only when every testable consequence of its FRs is covered by at least one passing Xaravel Test.
The Fidelity Review checks that each Xaravel Test verifies the behaviour it claims to.
The matchers cover every PHPUnit assertion used by the Upstream test suite at the Baseline Pin. A scan run with FR-1 lists them, and CI reports any that aren't covered.
`assertSame` follows PHP `===`, including array key order and value types. `assertEquals` follows PHP `==`.
`expectException` ends the test at the throw, as PHPUnit does.
PHPUnit `createMock` goes through `@xaravel/mockery`.
Each of these rules is verified by its own Xaravel Tests.

**Ported Tests.** - **Location:** `packages/<c>/tests/ported/<Upstream test path>.test.ts`. When sprint planning splits one Upstream file across Stories, each slice is its own file, `<Upstream test path>/<slice>.test.ts`. Exactly one open Story owns each Ported Test file. - **Declaration:** only through `portedTest('<Test ID>', { case?, dataset? }, async function () { ... })` from `@xaravel/assert`. `this` is the `case` TestCase instance (AD-25). - **Variants:** from the Test Inventory's `backends`, never declared by the test. The runner selects one with `XARAVEL_VARIANT`. - **Assertions:** only through `@xaravel/assert`. Importing `expect` from `bun:test` under `tests/ported` is a lint error. The assertion floor (FR-113) compares the multiset of assertion kinds recorded in the Inventory. - **Adapted assertions:** each changed assertion line carries `// adapted:DIV-<n>.<clause>`, and every Divergence Record numbers its adaptation clauses. - **Xaravel Tests:** `xaravelTest('XT-<c>-<n>', '<FR consequence>', fn)`.

**Data files (JSONL, sorted).** - **Expectations:** sharded to mirror the Ported Test files, at `conformance/expectations/<component>/<ported test file path>.jsonl`. Each line is one Test ID × Variant, with fields `id`, `variant`, `status`, `reason`, `adapted` and `escalation`. Parallel Stories therefore never edit the same shard. CI checks that each `(id, variant)` appears exactly once across shards. - **Test Inventory:** `conformance/inventory/<component>.jsonl`, with fields `id`, `component`, `kind`, `backends`, `hash`, `assertions`, `oracle` and `source`. `oracle` maps each Variant to the Upstream outcome the baseline recorded (`pass`, `fail` or `skip`). - **Variants:** a closed vocabulary in `conformance/variants`: `none`, `sqlite`, `pgsql`, `redis`, and `<driver>@<backend>` (`queue-database@pgsql`, `session-redis@redis`, …).

**Upstream snapshot.** `conformance/upstream/{framework,ai,mcp,boost}/` is read-only, at the tag in `conformance/baseline-pin`, synced by `bun run upstream:sync`. The Inventory's `source` field is a path into it plus a line range.

**Oracle.** - **Image:** a Docker image (PHP 8.5.11, Laravel at the Pin, committed `composer.lock`). - **Batch run:** one Infrastructure run per Pin generates fixtures for every Differential Test ID, from inputs extracted mechanically into `conformance/oracle/requests/` (Protected). - **New inputs:** for Xaravel Differential suites, and for datasets the batch missed, a Story commits `conformance/oracle-requests/<story-id>.jsonl`. Fidelity Review checks each request against Upstream. The Oracle workflow runs on the Story's PR and commits fixtures to the Story branch under `conformance/fixtures/<c>/`. It acts as the `xaravel-oracle` GitHub App, and each fixture carries an Ed25519 signature over (request hash, output). - **Fixture protection:** fixtures are protected by signature, not by path. The verification key is in Protected `conformance/oracle/oracle.pub`, and the private key exists only in the Oracle job. CI fails any fixture whose signature doesn't verify. `conformance/fixtures/` is excluded from CODEOWNERS.

**API-surface parity.** The Oracle exports, via PHP Reflection, every public Upstream class member (name, static, parameter names, defaults, nullability) to `conformance/api-surface/<c>.jsonl`. CI diffs that against each package's `.d.ts` and shows missing, renamed and extra members per Component on the dashboard. An extra member needs an entry in `conformance/api-surface/additions.jsonl` citing an FR or a DIV, and a missing member needs an entry in `conformance/api-surface/exceptions.jsonl` citing a DIV or a `deferred:` item. Both files are Protected. The diff is reported on every PR. It gates only the acceptance of a Component's last Epic, which requires zero unexplained members. Libraries outside the Test Inventory (phpdotenv, Inflector, Carbon, prompts, the Symfony surfaces, Monolog) get Oracle Differential Xaravel Tests in their owning Epic (AD-22).

**`blocked-by:<c>`.** It is valid only if the harness run fails with `BlockedByComponentError(<c>)`. That error is raised when a token, alias or FQCN owned by `<c>` (per the component map) is resolved and `<c>` is not installed.
**Generator references.** Generator Ported Tests (FR-71) compare against reference files in `conformance/fixtures/generators/` (Protected).
**Fidelity Review.** Its verdicts are GitHub PR reviews from at least two distinct reviewer identities. The done check counts approvals by identity.

**Grader isolation.** The harness, `@xaravel/assert` and `@xaravel/mockery` import no graded package. The matchers implement PHP `==` / `===` themselves and detect `PhpArray` and PHP props by `Symbol.for` brand. `@xaravel/assert` freezes its exports and prototypes on load. Frames are opened only through the runtime's global protocol. The harness runs `bun test` with the Protected root `bunfig.toml` and fails if any package-level `bunfig.toml` exists.
**Boost framework mode.** It reads all of this read-only.

**The list.** `conformance/protected-paths` (globs, itself Protected) is mirrored into `CODEOWNERS` with the Maintainer as owner. It covers: - in `conformance/`: everything except `expectations/`, `escalations/`, `oracle-requests/` and the signed `fixtures/`; - `decisions/`, `PORTING.md` and `stories/`; - `.github/`; - `tools/`; - `packages/assert`, `packages/mockery` and `packages/contracts` (contracts after Phase 1); - the root `package.json`, `bun.lock`, the root `bunfig.toml`, the root `tsconfig*.json` and `tsconfig.base.json`, `.oxlintrc.json`, `.gitattributes`, `.bun-version` and the root `LICENSE`. Package `tsconfig.json` files are generated and checked (AD-2). - the agent instructions and tooling: `AGENTS.md`, `**/CLAUDE.md` in any letter case (none may exist; one would stop Claude Code reading `AGENTS.md`), and `.claude/` (the settings, hooks and skills agents run, such as `bmad-build-auto`).

**Enforcement.** A GitHub ruleset on `main` requires the `protected-paths` and `ratchet` checks. They come from workflows pinned to the default branch (`pull_request_target`, which treats the PR diff as data only), so a PR cannot change its own checks. A change to a Protected Path needs Maintainer Code Owner review. That review is the Infrastructure Story approval and replaces any label.

**Permissions.** Workflows default to `permissions: contents: read`. Write scopes are granted per job to the Oracle, dashboard and release jobs only. Agents push with an identity limited to `story/*` branches, with no ruleset bypass.
**Disabling lint.** An `oxlint-disable` of any rule this spine names fails CI.

**Story manifest.** Story files are `stories/<story-id>.md`, written by sprint planning. CI reads `test_ids:` and `component:` from the **base branch**. A Story branch is named `story/<story-id>`. A Test ID may be listed by at most one open Story. CI fails a PR that changes Expectations lines or `portedTest` blocks whose IDs are not in its `test_ids`.
**Unexpected passes.** An unexpected pass of a Test ID owned by no open Story is a warning, and a bot opens a promotion PR. One owned by another open Story fails only that Story's next run.

**Planning PRs.** A `planning/*` branch may change tooling, docs, decisions and planning records, but never `packages/**` or `conformance/expectations/**`: framework code and grader data change only through `story/*` branches. The ownership check enforces this (decisions/MAINT-2026-10-17-epic-1-items.md). Through Phase 0 only, a retrospective fix on `planning/retro-<N>-*` (N ≤ 8) may change `packages/**`, never Expectations (decisions/MAINT-2026-10-16-unattended-orchestrator.md, amendment 2026-10-18).

**Bot PRs.** Quarantine and promotion bots push `bot/*` branches as their own App identity. The ownership check exempts them when they change only Expectations `status` values, and they open `ESC-bot-<n>` Escalations.

**Escalations.** An agent writes `conformance/escalations/ESC-<story-id>-<n>.md`, with frontmatter `test_ids`, `proposed` and `evidence`. The ruling is `decisions/ESC-<story-id>-<n>.md` with `decision: approved | rejected`. An Escalation counts as approved only when its decision file exists.
**Worktree key.** The harness takes the first 8 hex characters of SHA-256 over the worktree path plus its git worktree creation id.
**Postgres:** databases `xaravel_test_<key>[_<name>]`, recreated at the start of every full run. Tests drop only names that match this pattern.
**SQLite:** files under the worktree's `.cache/`.
**Redis:** one `redis-server` per worktree, on a unix socket in `.cache/` with no persistence. Tests may `flushdb`, and no harness prefix is injected. In CI, each job's own service is its server.
**One runner per worktree.** A lock file `.cache/harness.lock` keeps out a second runner in the same worktree.

**Reference environment (optional).** `.devcontainer/` is the Linux reference environment: Bun at `.bun-version`, `redis-server` at CI's Redis version inside the workspace (for the rule above), and a Postgres sidecar from CI's image. It is never required: every harness, tool and done check runs natively on macOS and Linux (NFR-1, PRD OQ-9, Story 2.2), where a backend that isn't running is `NOT-RUN`. Its pins are the Stack table's and CI's, checked mechanically. The workspace, or at least `.cache/`, lives on a container volume, not a host bind mount, so the Redis socket and the harness's I/O work. The container gets no Docker socket: the Oracle and Inventory jobs run in CI or on the host. A post-alpha engine (MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, memcached, Beanstalkd, DynamoDB Local) gets its sidecar from the Phase 9 Story that brings its driver; an amd64-only image is an optional Compose profile. A worktree used both inside and outside the container has two keys, and so two sets of databases.

**Scope of a Story.** A Story changes only `packages/<its component>/**`, its own Expectations lines, its own `oracle-requests` and its own escalations. CI checks the PR's paths against the Story's `component:`.
**Needs in another package.** They become a dependent Story on that package's Epic, which unblocks the requester through `blocked-by`.
**Contracts.** A missing or changed contract after Phase 1 goes through an Escalation.

**Large classes.** A large class may be split into method-group modules (`src/<Class>/<group>.ts`), merged onto the class through interface declaration merging. The class file stays the single public export.

**Per PR (linux-x64):** lint, typecheck, the protected-paths, ownership and dependency-graph checks, the Ratchet over the AD-2 reverse-dependency closure of the changed packages, and a full run of the Story's `test_ids` on every Variant.
**Merge queue:** required on `main`. It runs the full Ratchet on all alpha Variants, regenerates and checks `async-surface.json`, and runs the API-surface diff.

**Nightly:** the full matrix on linux and macOS, x64 and arm64. macOS jobs install Postgres and Redis natively, because service containers are Linux-only. The Oracle determinism re-check also runs nightly.
**Auto-quarantine:** a test that fails on `main` and then passes on rerun is quarantined by a bot PR to `expectations/`, which also opens an Escalation.
**Dependencies:** `bun audit` runs in every PR.
**Dashboard:** published to GitHub Pages from `main`.
**Branch protection:** linear history.
